source.citation: Matson KJE, Russ DE, Kathe C, et al. Single cell atlas of spinal cord injury in mice reveals a pro-regenerative signature in spinocerebellar neurons. Nature Communications 13, 5628 (2022).

license.appliesTo: Article and included source-data material unless a separate credit line states otherwise
license.rightsBoundary: The GEO processed files are publicly downloadable, but no accession-specific redistribution licence was located. Raw source files are not bundled; this release retains only factual identifiers and source-derived counts.

articleSupplementReferences.scope: Top 20 ranked genes for 39 source types; this release deterministically retains all ranks 1–20 for the 17 neuronal families and no absent score or p-value.

scope.spinalRegion: L2–S1 lumbar spinal cord distal to a thoracic injury

experimentalDesign.tissue: L2–S1 lumbar spinal cord with proximal dorsal and ventral roots attached
experimentalDesign.injuryTissueRelation: Sequenced lumbar tissue was below and distal to the T9 lesion site
experimentalDesign.sequencingPlatform: 10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell Kit v2; article reports Illumina HiSeq 3000 while GEO reports HiSeq 2500
experimentalDesign.analysis: Cell Ranger 2.2.0, Velocyto and Seurat v3
experimentalDesign.selectionBoundary: For snRNA-seq, three mice representative of each time point were selected from a larger kinematically assessed cohort; captured nuclei are not a tissue-prevalence census.
experimentalDesign.exclusionBoundary: The paper reports excluding mice with visible hindlimb movement during contusion, bone-hit injuries, kinematic outliers, or behavioral-data loss. The 15 sequenced mice are a selected terminal cross-sectional sample, not repeated longitudinal measurements.

rareStateEvidence.label: RAG-expressing neuronal state · independent neuronal cluster 23
established: The independent neuronal clustering identified a rare RAG-expressing state after injury.
RNAscope detected Sprr1a and Atf3 from 1 week through 6 weeks post injury.
Most RAG-expressing neurons were excitatory; a small subset expressed Shox2, while co-expression with Chat or Vsx2 was not detected in the reported assay.
Separate tracing and viral-labeling experiments support a major spinocerebellar projection-neuron contribution and post-injury axon/collateral remodeling.
rareStateEvidence.boundary: The RAG state is not one of the 17 label-transfer population records, and the sequencing, RNAscope and tracing observations are not same-cell joins. Spinocerebellar neurons are projection neurons, not local interneurons. Structural remodeling does not by itself establish behavioral recovery or synaptic connectivity.

globalMissingEvidence.reason: The processed metadata contains no per-nucleus physical coordinate.
snRNA-seq labels and tissue images do not provide reconstructable single-neuron arbors.
Tracing and sequencing were not performed as a same-cell linkage.
Axon remodeling and proximity do not identify synaptic partners.
No transform registers source nuclei or histology to the project reference anatomy.
Captured nucleus counts have different library denominators and are not a tissue census.
The time-course and remodeling observations do not establish that a population is necessary or sufficient for behavioral recovery.

hardBoundaries: All 17 neuronal labels remain in the Matson/GSE172167 source namespace; exact identity to Russ, Sathyamurthy, morphology, anatomy or SCI evidence records is zero.
The 16 non-motor source populations are spinal-neuron populations, not 16 confirmed local interneuron types; local versus ascending projection status is unresolved at the record level.

Captured nucleus counts and shares describe this processed dataset only and must not be displayed as biological prevalence, cell loss or expansion without the source study's compositional analysis and validation.
The RAG state, molecular population labels, RNAscope cells, dextran-labelled neurons and virally labelled spinocerebellar neurons remain separate observations unless the paper directly links them.
No coordinate, morphology, complete axon, synapse, atlas placement or same-cell cross-modal join may be inferred from this release.
A missing measurement remains an explicit gap and is not evidence that the corresponding biological feature is absent.
